summary: The architecture (pure-probe / injectable-resolver split modeled on lib/solomon/conduct-probes.js) is the correct and idiomatic choice for this repo, and it makes the FR-7 two-sided requirement achievable without a database. But TS-1..TS-11 as authored do NOT deliver per-class two-sided validation: T3 has no firing positive at all, T1's and T2's negatives share their positives' assumptions and are satisfied by a broken detector, three scenarios (TS-7/9/10) are typed 'integration' and are UNRUNNABLE in this repo's CI today, and the SD's own headline risk (the unwired cron) has ZERO test scenarios. All 12 required additions are additive test scenarios plus one file rename; no architectural change is needed. CONDITIONAL_PASS to enter EXEC with R1-R12 folded into the PRD test_scenarios.

part_1_two_sided_per_class.requirement: FR-7: for EACH of T1/T2/T3 a seeded known-trend MUST fire AND a flat series MUST NOT, in the same suite.
part_1_two_sided_per_class.verdict: NOT MET for any of the three classes as authored.

T1_REPEAT_QUESTION.defect: TS-2 varies ONLY the timestamp from TS-1. Both fixtures assert 'two SAME-CLASS messages'. A clustering function broken in the over-collapse direction (every message lands in one class — the most likely failure mode, since FR-2 concedes the clustering is NEW WORK and chairman-sms-exchanges.js:43-46 explicitly REFUSES similarity matching) passes TS-1 (fires) AND passes TS-2 (24h rule still suppresses). Both sides green, detector wrong.
T1_REPEAT_QUESTION.missing: A discriminating negative: two messages 24h+ apart but of DIFFERENT question-class must NOT fire. Also missing: n=1 single message; and an OUTBOUND-only pair 24h+ apart (FR-2 says INBOUND chairman SMS — the direction filter is untested).
T1_REPEAT_QUESTION.note: FR-2's own acceptance_criteria list has the same hole — it enumerates the 24h boundary both ways but never a different-class case.

T2_RECURRENCE_AFTER_FIX.positive: TS-3 (pre-fix occurrences only in retention_archive) — adequate as a firing case, but see Part 3: it cannot prove what it claims.
T2_RECURRENCE_AFTER_FIX.negative: TS-4 (a class that appeared once and never returned) — DEGENERATE.
T2_RECURRENCE_AFTER_FIX.defect: TS-4's fixture is n=1. Any detector requiring >=2 occurrences passes it trivially without ever consulting the fix timestamp. T2 therefore degenerates to 'count >= 2' and TS-3 still passes. The 'after-fix' pivot — the entire semantic content of T2 — is unexercised.
T2_RECURRENCE_AFTER_FIX.missing: R3: a class with 2+ occurrences that ALL fall BEFORE the fix, then silence, must NOT fire. That is the only negative that proves the fix timestamp is a pivot rather than decoration. R4: union-dedup — one logical occurrence present in BOTH retention_archive and session_coordination (they overlap 2026-07-24..2026-08-06 by archive-before-delete) must count ONCE. A naive concat union double-counts every row in the overlap and manufactures false T2 fires; no scenario covers it.

T3_LESSON_DISJUNCTION.negative: TS-6 (stable ratio, no drift candidate) — present.
T3_LESSON_DISJUNCTION.defect: TS-5 is not a firing positive. It asserts 'a series reading is emitted' and that a mismatched-span fixture fails an assertion. Neither is 'a seeded known-trend FIRES'. As written, T3 can ship with a drift detector that can never emit a candidate and the entire suite stays green — the exact one-sided failure FR-7 exists to prevent. This is the clearest and most serious FR-7 violation in the PRD.
T3_LESSON_DISJUNCTION.missing: R1: a seeded genuine drift series (ratio degrading across the window) that FIRES a T3 candidate. Also unexercised: FR-4 AC2 'emitted as a series reading, not a point verdict' has no scenario asserting multi-reading semantics via recursion-governor detectSustainedBreach(recent,{requiredConsecutive}); and FR-4 AC1 'T3 writes no value to issue_patterns.trend' — a hard LEAD condition C2 constraint — has NO test scenario at all.

cross_class_leakage.defect: No scenario asserts that a seed for one class does not satisfy another class's positive. With three classes emitting into one candidate array, expect(out).toHaveLength(1) alone is satisfiable by the wrong class firing.
cross_class_leakage.required: R12: every positive must assert the CLASS NAME, e.g. expect(out).toHaveLength(1); expect(out[0]).toMatchObject({ trigger: 'T1' }). Precedent: tests/unit/row-growth-detector.test.js:22-39 asserts trigger:'abs_spike' / 'growth_factor' by name for exactly this reason.

part_2_negative_fixture_independence.principle: FR-7 AC4 already states it ('negative fixtures built on a different assumption than the positive ones'), but no TS implements it. A control that inherits the flaw it controls passes while the answer is wrong.

recommended_construction_per_class.T1: Do NOT build the negative by editing the positive's timestamps (that keeps the clustering assumption fixed and only varies the axis the positive already varies). Build it on the CLASS axis instead: two messages 26h apart whose bodies are drawn from a DIFFERENT question-class than the specimen. This is a one-field delta on an axis the positive holds constant — the coordinator-belt-block.test.js:31 idiom ('same zero depth, ONE field different') and its meta-assertion at :55 that the controls differ by one field each. Keep TS-2 as a boundary test, but it is not the class's negative control.
recommended_construction_per_class.T2: Do NOT build the negative by deleting occurrences (n=1 tests arity, not recurrence). Build it on the TEMPORAL-ORDER axis: same occurrence count, same class, same fix event — only the ordering relative to the fix changes (all occurrences pre-fix). Positive varies 'where the rows live' (archive vs survivor); negative varies 'when they occur relative to the fix'. Different axes, so no shared assumption can green both.
recommended_construction_per_class.T3: Do NOT build the negative as an empty/absent series (that tests arity again). Build it on the VARIANCE axis: same number of readings, same extent, same numerator/denominator sources — only the values are flat. And build the positive on the same skeleton with a monotone degradation. Then add a third fixture varying the SPAN axis (TS-5's mismatched-span case) so span-correctness is independent of drift-detection.

third_arm_required.finding: TS-2/4/6 all expect 'No candidate', which conflates 'looked, found flat' with 'could not look'. conduct-probes.js:49-58 and :81-83 establish the repo's three-state contract: null/undefined => UNKNOWN, never PASS; 0 => PASS ('looked and found none'); the resolver returns null on ANY failure, never 0. Its test asserts this directly (conduct-probes.test.js:51-62, 'UNAVAILABLE: a resolver that cannot answer yields unknown, NEVER pass' — loops 4 broken clients asserting .not.toBe(VERDICT.PASS)).
third_arm_required.required: R6: add a THIRD ARM per class — unresolvable/null facts must yield UNKNOWN or propagate, never a silent no-fire. This is also the only test that would enforce PRD risk #6 ('the scan swallows a query error into an empty result'), which currently has a stated mitigation and zero scenarios.
third_arm_required.why_it_matters: Without it, a scan whose query silently fails produces exactly the same observable as a healthy flat window — and the run-receipt (FR-6) will still be written, so the liveness predicate stays green too. Two safeguards composing into invisibility.

control_on_the_controls.finding: Any assertion of ABSENCE (no fire, no forbidden import, no write) passes just as happily against an empty string or a vacuous slice.

TS3_correction.finding: TS-3 is typed 'unit' and its FR-3 acceptance says 'verified by a test that seeds a class present ONLY in retention_archive'. A PURE PROBE test cannot deliver this. The union lives in the RESOLVER (the IO half); a probe fed a pre-unioned facts bag proves nothing about which tables were read. As written TS-3 is satisfied by a resolver that reads session_coordination only, provided the fixture author hand-places the row in the facts bag.
TS3_correction.required: R5: recast TS-3 as a RESOLVER test using a fake supabase double that RECORDS the table names passed to .from() — still pure, still zero DB. Assert (a) from() was called with BOTH 'retention_archive' and 'session_coordination', and (b) a row present only in the archive double survives into the facts bag. Fixture idiom: the 4-line db(result) double at lib/solomon/conduct-probes.test.js:23-28, extended to push table names onto an array. This converts an unprovable claim into a pure, CI-runnable one.

part_4_unwired_cron_anti_pattern.answer_to_how_do_you_test_a_cron_is_wire: Three layers, all cheap: (1) the classifier-visible FILENAME (R8) makes the gate see the file at all; (2) the comment-stripped workflow unit test with a tampered control (R7) is the blocking, durable regression guard; (3) the real scheduled run leaving a receipt row (FR-8, already in the PRD) is the one-time proof that secrets and permissions actually resolve on a runner. The PRD currently has only layer 3, which is exactly why the eva precedent was invisible.

required_additions.item: Add a T3 FIRING POSITIVE (seeded genuine drift series emits a T3 candidate). TS-5 is not one. Without this T3 ships one-sided and can never fire.
Add T1 discriminating negative: two messages 24h+ apart of DIFFERENT question-class must NOT fire. TS-2 varies only the timestamp and is green under an over-collapsing classifier.
Add T2 discriminating negative: 2+ occurrences ALL pre-fix, then silence, must NOT fire. TS-4's n=1 fixture never exercises the fix pivot.

Add T2 union-dedup scenario: one logical occurrence present in BOTH retention_archive and session_coordination (07-24..08-06 overlap) counts ONCE. A naive concat union manufactures false fires across the whole overlap.
Recast TS-3 as a RESOLVER test with a table-recording supabase double. A pure probe fed pre-unioned facts cannot prove the union read, which is TS-3's entire stated purpose.
Add a per-class THIRD ARM: unresolvable/null facts yield UNKNOWN or propagate, never a silent no-fire. Enforces the conduct-probes three-state contract and is the only cover for PRD risk #6.

Add TS-16 workflow-wiring unit test (comment-stripped active schedule, run-step entrypoint, exactly the two SUPABASE_* secrets, no POOLER/DATABASE_URL/PGHOST) WITH a tampered-body control, plus a detectInvocationPath(...).invoked === true assertion. Currently zero scenarios cover the SD's headline risk.

RENAME the entrypoint from trend-eyes-scan.mjs to a classifier-visible name (trend-eyes-sweep.mjs, or move under scripts/cron/). '-scan' is not in AUTONOMOUS_SUFFIX_RE, so as named the script inherits the exact eva blind spot and INVOCATION_PATH_PROOF will never see it. Also add a loop-contract-registry entry.

Add static-source forbidden-token tests, bounded-region + tampered control + non-vacuous-slice control: (a) no pg / DATABASE_URL / SUPABASE_POOLER_URL (FR-1 AC3, currently untested); (b) no write to issue_patterns.trend (FR-4 AC1, LEAD condition C2, currently untested).

Resolve TS-7/9/10 placement: recast as pure payload-contract tests on an exported buildCandidateRow() (four NOT NULL columns + CHECK vocabularies, two-sided via a tampered payload); keep any true-insert variant as *.db.test.js with an explicit non-execution comment; and name FR-8's real run as the live insert-contract proof. As typed they run nowhere.

Suite placement constraint: tests/unit/solomon/trend-eyes-probes.test.js. NOT *.db.test.js, NOT tests/integration/, NOT wrapped in describeDb. Use toContain(quoted) for SUPABASE_* tokens so audit-db-test-guards.mjs does not flag the file.
Every positive must assert the CLASS NAME (toMatchObject({trigger:'T1'})), not merely toHaveLength(1), so one class's seed cannot silently satisfy another's positive.

what_is_already_good: The pure-probe / injectable-resolver split (FR-1) is the correct repo idiom and is what makes per-class two-sided validation possible with zero DB — this is the single most important thing the PRD gets right.
FR-7 AC4 already articulates the different-assumption requirement for negative fixtures; it just needs scenarios that implement it.
TS-11 (MACHINE_TELEMETRY_CATEGORIES non-membership) is well-targeted and matches an existing, battle-tested pin at emit-feedback-telemetry-audience.test.js:41-43.
TS-8 (liveness predicate returns alarm:true for null/stale) correctly copies the gauge-runner triple and is genuinely two-sided in intent.
FR-8's refusal to accept a merged workflow file as evidence is exactly right and empirically justified — I verified both eva precedent scripts return invoked:false with zero triggers.
